newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan supermarkets to use U.S. electronic coupons.
newsitem.headline: Japan supermarkets to use U.S. electronic coupons.

text.p: Japan's leading supermarket operators Jusco Co Ltd and Seiyu Ltd said on Thursday they will try out out a U.S. electronic coupon system until December.
Jusco said it began using Florida-based Catalina Marketing Corp's electronic coupon system in 10 of its outlets this month.
The system is connected to cash registers and issues discount coupons every time a customer buys certain products.
Seiyu said it would adopt the system in six of its outlets in the Tokyo area from July, and four in western Japan from August. It expects to apply the system in all 202 Seiyu outlets in 1998.
"This is a new system in Japan, and it is a good way to distinguish us from other stores in the region," a Seiyu spokeswoman said.
"The system applies to products with high purchase frequency, and we hope it appeals to customers as they get discount coupons each time they shop," a Jusco spokesman said.
The Japanese daily Nihon Keizai Shimbun said on Thursday that Ito-Yokado Co Ltd and other supermarkets were also considering the use of an electronic coupon system.
Ito-Yokado was not immediately available for comment.
